observations: Sony PlayStation 4 Slim console with a Spider-Man themed skin/wrap.
Console is wrapped in protective plastic film.
One boxed DualShock 4 wireless controller; box appears to be a common retail replacement or clone style.
TV screen shows PS4 dashboard with several game tiles: Red Dead Redemption 2, Ghost of Tsushima, Mortal Kombat 11, etc.
Game icons on the dashboard show 'lock' symbols in photo 0 and photo 2.
Watermark 'JAYCYPHER GAMES' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' present on all photos.
Console is powered on and connected to a TCL television.

claims.evidence: The dashboard shows games, but they have lock icons, which usually indicates the licenses are not active or the exploit is not running. No proof of GoldHEN or Debug Settings is visible.
The slim form factor is clearly visible in photo 1.
At least 7 game tiles are visible on the dashboard in photo 0 and 2.

risks.risk: The console may not be on a jailbreakable firmware (9.00 or 11.00 or lower).
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen showing the System Software version.

risks.risk: The controller may be a third-party clone rather than original Sony hardware.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the back label of the controller.
A photo of the 'Storage' settings screen.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video of a disc being inserted, recognized, and ejected.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

proof_requests: Photo of Settings > System > System Information showing the firmware version.
Photo of the 'Storage' menu showing the hard drive size.
Photo of the 'Settings' menu showing 'Debug Settings' or 'GoldHEN' to prove the hack is active.
Photo of the back of the controller to verify authenticity.
response.reason: The 'hacked' status is the primary value driver but is unverified; the lock icons on the games suggest the exploit is either missing or non-functional. Firmware version must be confirmed.
